title: Reviewer's Heuristics
blurb: A handful of questions catch most flaws in a code review. Match each reviewer's rule-of-thumb to the class of bug it's designed to surface.

levels.title: L1 · Ask these while you read
levels.prompt: Match each review question to what it catches.

left.label: Trace every piece of request input to where it's used
Is there an ownership check, not just a login?
Does validation happen on the server, not only in the browser?
On error, does the code deny by default?

right.label: injection — SQL, command, or XSS (untrusted input reaching a sink)
broken access control — e.g. IDOR, reading another user's record by changing an id
client-trust bypass — the attacker skips the browser and posts raw values
fail-open — an exception skips a security check and the code proceeds anyway

levels.explain: Tracing request input to its sink finds injection. Asking for an ownership check (not just a login) finds IDOR / broken access control. Insisting validation runs server-side finds client-trust bypasses. Checking that errors deny by default finds fail-open bugs.

failStates.title: Ownership is about access, not injection
failStates.explain: Injection is untrusted input becoming code — you catch it by tracing input to sinks. The ownership question catches broken access control (IDOR): a logged-in user reaching data that isn't theirs.

failStates.title: That's the fail-open question
failStates.explain: "Deny by default on error" catches fail-open bugs (a thrown exception skipping a check). Client-trust bypass is caught by requiring server-side validation.
